Echoooo echooo echoo echoo... Oh look, it's empty, there's nothing in this movie. 2 hours of wandering around the woods carrying the rin- horcrux, that makes its wearer go mad. I didn't remember much about this movie and now I know why: there is nothing to be remembered about it. Endless static shot reverse-shot dialogue scenes. Characters walking from point A to point B in silence and with no music. If there was a plot I already forgot it again. I don't think I've used the phrase "waste of time" in any of my reviews, but this was a waste of time. I kept waiting for anything interesting to happen and it never came. There is no way that the two parter ending is justified, based on this movie. Further evidence that Hogwarts is what makes Harry Potter good. This isn't more "mature", it's just boring.

Rien n'est bien géré, les scènes se suivent d'une manière artificielle si mauvaise, on explore pas la psychologie des personnages mais on nous envoie à la gueule des éléments auxquels on doit croire sans rien établir, la peur de Ron sur la relation potentielle d'Harry et Hermione en est le meilleur exemple pcq avant ça on les voit juste marcher ensemble, les scènes qui suivent sont meilleurs, la danse est une bonne scène mais c'est pas dingue non plus surtout que Hermione et Harry pourraient juste donner des faits MAIS NON. Side note: this account does not endorse the hateful bigotry of JKR in any medium, shape or form. This was probably a hard book to adapt, but their approach doesn't do it any favors. Some scenes are very literally translated to screen, with tons of exposition and explanation between them removed. I feel like we get the worst of both worlds here. Lots of wandering around aimlessly in the woods and bickering, without the benefit of a compelling mystery (which even the book didn't convincingly sell). Perhaps the worst part is the acting. Almost everyone looks bored at this point, and they're given only the most banal dialogue to keep the plot moving. You'd hardly believe these kids are supposed to be best friends of six years. The depiction of magic here is also quite uninspiring; wands are basically just guns.

I just hate what they’ve done with Ron throughout the series he’s gone from my favorite character in the first movie to the absolute most annoying, headache inducing person whenever he’s on screen. Whining, complaining, being jealous, every second he’s on screen is excruciating and exhausting to watch. And what’s with Ron disappearing for a whole ass month? And he just comes back 20 minutes later like nothing happened. The dance with Harry and Hermione was just so incredibly awkward, the whole movie just feels like a slog. This movie was 2 and a half hours but it felt like 4. I also get that the movie is supposed to have a somber mood and depressing mood but god man everything is so gray and uninteresting to look at. The whole movie just feels like an exposition dump and I wanted to turn the movie off the whole time.

Movie three of four. I am le tired. I can’t tell if the movies are truly getting worse or if they are really are just becoming less enjoyable. This one has a significantly different structure from the first movies, and I don’t think I particularly care for it. I don’t think the strength of these stories are in the main three’s friendship, but that’s what we are stuck with for the majority of the Deathly Hallows Part 1. It drags. I mean, I’m glad and all that the trope of the teacher of the dark arts being the villain is finally put to bed. But it’s not that interesting. Maybe I’ll have more thoughts later. Shout out to Cho’s split second cameo on the train. Asian representation! /s

Siento que esta película simplemente no funciona conmigo. Entiendo lo que intenta hacer y por qué tiene un tono mucho más serio, pero se me hace demasiado pesada y bastante menos entretenida que las anteriores. La idea de tener a Harry, Ron y Hermione prácticamente solos durante gran parte de la película podría haberme encantado, pero el ritmo hace que algunos momentos se me hagan eternos. Hay escenas que visualmente son preciosas y otras que me parecen muy buenas, pero me cuesta sentir esa emoción que tenía con las primeras entregas. También creo que aquí se nota muchísimo el cambio de tono de la saga. Todo es gris, triste y oscuro, y personalmente echo muchísimo de menos la magia, el humor y la sensación de estar descubriendo el mundo de Hogwarts que tenían las primeras. No me parece una película horrible, porque tiene momentos muy potentes y la historia sigue siendo interesante, pero como experiencia me resulta bastante fría y aburrida en comparación con las demás.
